she: used to refer to a female person or animal already mentioned
She left the office early to catch her train.
points: indicates or suggests something as likely or true
The evidence points to a sudden change in weather patterns.
more: to a greater degree or extent
Careful listeners remember song lyrics more clearly than plain speech.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
until: up to the point in time that something happens
It worked until it did not.
pushed: pressed against something to move it away
The old car was pushed off the road after it broke down.
aside: to one side; out of consideration
She set her worries aside and focused on finishing the project.
make: to produce, create or cause something
Good lighting can make a small room feel much larger.
way: As a way of saving money, it is easy to copy and abandon.
paddle-steamers: boats powered by steam engines that turn large paddle wheels
tàu chạy hơi nước có bánh guồng
Paddle-steamers once carried wool down the river to the coast.
taking: getting hold of, removing, or carrying something
Taking notes during the lecture helped her remember the key points.
wool: the soft hair of sheep, used to make fabric
She knitted a warm sweater from local sheep's wool.
clip: a short extract from a film, video, or piece of music
She shared a funny clip from the concert on social media.
adelaide: Her cousin moved to Adelaide for a new job last year.
late: near the end of a period of time, or after the expected time
They arrived late because of heavy traffic downtown.
19th: coming after the eighteenth in a series; number 19
This is her 19th trip to Paris this year.
century: a period of one hundred years
The tradition has been passed down for more than a century.
according: in a way that agrees with or depends on something
Pay varies according to experience and the hours worked.
peak: the highest point or greatest level reached by something
Electricity demand reaches its peak on the hottest summer days.
western: relating to the west, especially Western countries
In much of Western Europe, the share of older people rose slowly.
murdi: part of the name of an Indigenous Australian regional assembly
Murdi Paaki represents communities across western New South Wales.
paaki: part of the name of an Indigenous Australian regional assembly
Murdi Paaki represents Indigenous communities across the region.
regional: relating to a particular area rather than the whole country
The regional airport handles far fewer flights than the capital's.
assembly: the process of fitting parts together, or a gathering of people
The factory's assembly line produces hundreds of cars each day.
mpra: abbreviation for the Murdi Paaki Regional Assembly, an Indigenous body
The MPRA represents Indigenous communities across western New South Wales.
creation: the act of bringing something new into existence
sự tạo ra, sự sáng tạo
The creation of the national park took nearly a decade of negotiation.
lore: a body of traditional knowledge and beliefs held by a community
tri thức truyền thống, luật tục
The elders passed down their lore through generations of storytelling.
governing: ruling or controlling a country, organization, or activity
A small committee is governing the club until new elections.
use: to employ something for a particular purpose
What cannot be coined is a reason to use them.
helped: gave assistance to; past tense of help
Volunteers helped clear debris after the storm passed.
spiritual: relating to the soul or to deep, non-physical beliefs
thuộc về tâm linh, tinh thần
Many people find spiritual comfort in nature and quiet reflection.
political: relating to government, public affairs, or politics
The debate quickly turned into a political argument about taxes.
social: relating to society or to spending time with other people
She enjoys an active social life with many close friends.
ceremonial: relating to or used in formal rituals or ceremonies
The elders wore ceremonial robes during the ancient ritual.
relationships: the ways in which two or more people or things are connected
Building strong relationships with customers is vital for small businesses.
between: in the space or time separating two things
The old road runs between two small villages in the valley.
groups: put people or things into sets sharing a characteristic
The teacher groups the students by ability before each project.
across: from one side of something to the other
A narrow bridge stretches across the river near the old mill.
greater: larger in size, amount, or degree
Cities with greater population density often have better public transport.
food: any substance eaten to maintain life and growth
They stored enough food to last through the winter.
production: the process of making or growing something in large quantities
Production at the factory slowed after the machinery broke down.
consumption: the act of using up, eating, or drinking something
Household electricity consumption usually rises during the hottest months.
cultural: relating to the customs, arts, and social behaviour of a society
The festival celebrates the city's rich cultural heritage.
museum: a building where objects of historical, artistic or scientific interest are displayed
The children spent the afternoon exploring the science museum downtown.
popular: liked, supported, or used by many people
That café became popular with students soon after it opened.
tourists: plural of tourist; people travelling for pleasure
It would be wrong to see tourists only as a problem.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
facebook: She posted the news on Facebook within minutes of hearing it.
page: one side of a sheet of paper in a book or document
She turned the page slowly, savouring the final chapter.
records: written or stored accounts of facts or events
hồ sơ, dữ liệu ghi chép
The library keeps records of every book ever borrowed.
visits: goes to see a person or place
If part of the crowd visits in a different season, the pressure eases.
posts: items of content published online, such as on social media
She scrolled through dozens of posts before finding the article.
numerous: There are numerous reasons why the project was delayed.
videos: recordings of moving images, often with sound
Dramatic videos of the storm spread quickly online.
manager: a person who controls or organises a business or team
The new manager introduced several changes to the daily schedule.
bradley: a male given name belonging to a manager in the article
Bradley manages the heritage site for the local council.
hardy: These hardy shrubs can survive both drought and frost.
enthusiastic: showing strong excitement or interest in something
He gave an enthusiastic speech about the benefits of the plan.
advocate: a person who publicly supports a cause
người ủng hộ, người biện hộ
She became a leading advocate for children's education.
